newsitem.title: GERMANY: Honecker got fake reports on E.Germany - witness.
newsitem.headline: Honecker got fake reports on E.Germany - witness.

text.p: Erich Honecker, the disgraced ruler of former East Germany, regularly received embellished reports about conditions in the communist state from deputies who feared upsetting their boss, his secretary said on Monday.
Elli Kelm testified at the trial of four former East German leaders that Honecker was largely unaware of the conditions in East Germany because he was presented with distorted reports.

"They were strongly filtered or embellished," Kelm, 63, told the court. She said the instructions to falsify the reports came from Guenter Mittag, who oversaw the economy. "We didn't want to upset Honecker" with bad news, she said.
Honecker, who resigned in October 1989 shortly before the Berlin Wall collapsed, died in exile in Chile in 1994.
His successor Egon Krenz and three other former East German leaders have been on trial for the last year facing manslaughter charges in connection with shootings at the Berlin Wall.

Kelm also said she believed Erich Mielke, the head of the feared Stasi security police, even spied on Honecker. She said Mielke seemed to know about details contained in letters that were on Honecker's desk even before he had opened them.
